title: B-e2e: Playwright mobile driver specs + DEMO/decisions docs
e2e_result: FULL SUITE GREEN — `npm run e2e` (both projects) exit 0: 5 passed (35.4s). chromium 2/2 (AC1_CreateAndAssign, AC2_RealtimeCardMove) — NO regression from the getOrder unwrap (OrderCard/OrderDrawer now receive correct bare DTOs). mobile-driver 3/3: Driver_FullFlow_StartShiftToCompleteFixed_ShowsTotals (offer takeover ~324ms after assign, well under 2s; accept->arrive->start->complete fixed 250 CZK cash->Home shows 1 ride + 250 Kč), Driver_Decline_ReturnsOrderToNew (1.5s), Driver_OfflineArrive_QueuedThenDeliveredExactlyOnce (1.9s — queued badge shown offline + server still Accepted; reload after setOffline(false) drains the IDB queue; exactly ONE Arrived event). Two projects coexist over the one shared webServer harness. (An earlier full-run attempt hit a transient 'webServer exited early' from a stale Taxi.Api.exe holding :5249 left by an isolated debug run — cleared the port and the clean re-run passed 5/5.)
notes: Cheap checks all green: tsc clean, lint (--max-warnings 0) clean, vitest 627 passed (re-run AFTER the client.ts fix — still 627) and does NOT pick up e2e/driver.spec.ts (93 test files). Seed creds: dispatcher@demo.local/Demo1234!; driver used = driver2@demo.local/Demo1234! (Petr Svoboda) resolved to its driver-row id at runtime via listDrivers. Config project split: chromium project gains testIgnore:/driver.spec.ts/, new mobile-driver project (Pixel 5, geolocation granted) with testMatch:/driver.spec.ts/, same webServer array reused, chromium listed first. AC#5 exactly-once asserted by counting Arrived events on GET /orders/{id}/events (dispatcher token) == 1. Spec sequence: wait for arrive button visible WHILE ONLINE (so setOffline can't abort the in-flight reconcile fetch) -> setOffline(true) -> tap arrive (item queued, 'čeká na odeslání' badge visible in BOTH DriverQueueBar and ride PendingBadge -> assert .first() visible; server still Accepted) -> setOffline(false) -> page.reload() -> badge count 0 (queue drained) -> order Arrived, exactly one Arrived event. RELOAD MECHANISM RATIONALE: Playwright context.setOffline does NOT drop an already-open SignalR WebSocket in the brief offline window, so the hub never leaves 'connected' and the reconnect-drain (useQueueReplayOnReconnect fires only on a transition INTO 'connected') never triggers; a reload forces a cold hub connect that drains the IndexedDB-persisted queue on 'connected' — a faithful stand-in for the app reconnecting on real network restore (verified via trace: only 1 negotiate, no 2nd arrive POST, ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED on the queued arrive). Exactly-once still holds: the offline attempt never reached the server so there is nothing to double; the replay carries the same enqueue-time X-Idempotency-Key (B-queue) + server idempotency (A-idem). MINOR ROBUSTNESS SUGGESTION for reviewer (NOT a blocker): B-queue has no window 'online' event drain trigger; it relies solely on the hub reconnect-to-connected transition, so a brief network blip that fails a mutation fetch without dropping the WS leaves the item queued until the next hub reconnect. X-Idempotency-Key minted at enqueue (B-queue) + server idempotency (A-idem) dedupe. Manual ACs: AC#1 installability documented in DEMO.md §11 (npm run build && npx vite preview -> DevTools Application/Lighthouse PWA incl. maskable icon) because devOptions.enabled:false means SW/manifest never activate under npm run dev; AC#3 push background half deferred to assignment 05 (DEMO.md §12 + decisions.md). CROSS-WI BUG FIXED (route back to B-ride owner): the E2E surfaced a genuine B-ride/UC-002 data-path bug — web/src/shared/api/client.ts getOrder() did NOT unwrap the { order: OrderDetailDto } envelope that GET /orders/{id} returns (GetOrderResponse), so useRideRestore stored { order:{...} } and the ride screen rendered blank pickup/phone + NO action button (trace evidence: GET body was {"order":{...,"status":"Accepted"...}}; screenshot showed empty ride layout). Fixed minimally in web scope by unwrapping .order in getOrder — the exact laneB11 CreateOrderResponse {order} precedent. All 4 call sites (useRideRestore, useTransitionQueue.reconcileOrder, OrderDrawer, OrderCard) consume a bare DTO, so the unwrap is universally correct (OrderCard/OrderDrawer were also silently getting undefined coords/fields). tsc clean + 627 vitest + 48 targeted tests green after the fix. Envelope audit also confirmed GetMySummaryResponse is BARE (client type matches) so the totals-chip assertion is safe; GetMyOrdersResponse is enveloped but is History-only, not on this WI's path.
verification_output: npm run tsc: clean. npm run lint: clean (0 warnings). npm run test: 93 files / 627 tests passed, e2e excluded.
blocked_on: AC#2 start-shift sub-step is NOT UI-driveable: DriverHomePage builds the home vehicle selector ONLY from GET /drivers/me currentVehicleId, and POST /drivers/me/offline nulls current_vehicle_id; there is no driver-facing vehicle-list endpoint, so an offline driver cannot pick a vehicle to start a shift through the UI. The full-flow spec therefore drives AC#2 from the online precondition (driver2 kept Free via API) and proves offer->accept->arrive->start->complete(fixed)->Home totals through the real UI. This is a B-home gap to route back to B-home; NOT worked around by DB-fabricating an unreachable Offline-with-vehicle state. Documented in DEMO.md §10 and decisions.md UC-003 assumption 3.
